was: Gee Creek Campground: 47 drive-in sites on A and B loops, concrete pads 40-108 ft (some north-side Loop A sites need leveling). No hookups; potable water pumps, central bathhouse with hot showers, table/fire ring/grill per site. Seasonal (approx Apr 1-Oct 31), reservable online (reserve.tnstateparks.com). NOTE: park announced infrastructure renovation closing the campground fall 2026, reopening anticipated spring 2027. was: Primitive 8-site FCFS campground along Tumbling Creek near Ocoee #3 Lake, Cherokee NF (Ocoee/Big Frog Mountain region). No reservations (not on recreation.gov). Mostly small RVs/vans/cars, but the first couple of sites fit medium RVs/trailers with room to turn around (23-ft feasible). No designated pads, no hookups, no toilets/water/tables; max 5 people per site; bear-proof food storage required. Access via gravel FR 45/FR 221; easiest approach is paved Grassy Creek Rd off Hwy 68 then ~2 mi on FR 221 — passable by a normal vehicle. Open year-round. FCFS — not on recreation.gov. --Claude

was: USFS Cherokee NF, Tellico Plains Ranger District. ~11-12 small primitive sites (gravel pads) on the Tellico River along paved Tellico River Rd (FR210). Picnic table, fire ring, lantern post, vault toilets; NO potable water, NO hookups. RV + tent (small rigs; sibling sites on this road fit ~25-26 ft). FCFS only -- no reservations on recreation.gov; pay on-site via Scan & Pay QR, ~$10/night. Seasonal, roughly mid-spring to fall (2025 open date May 22). Currently operating per 2025/26 USFS schedule. --Claude

Drive-in; FS notes 'Sites 2 and 3 are ideal for mid-sized campers and trailers' and sites 4-6 for mid/smaller rigs (firsthand report of a 25-ft truck camper; low branches a caveat for tall rigs). Vault toilets, no potable water; bear food storage. FCFS only, open year-round. Operated by Cherokee National Forest (Tellico River Ranger District). --Claude

was: The original Buffalo River outfitter, family-run for 35 years at Bell Bridge on Hwy 13 just north of Waynesboro. Its North and South campgrounds have 30/50-amp electric-and-water RV sites along over a mile of river frontage (a few septic sites for monthly stays), free showers and restrooms, a camp store, and canoe and kayak floats. Open April to October. First come, first served with no reservations; cash only, paid at the gate or to a camping assistant; the gates are never locked; no generators. Office and South Campground at 2505 Waynesboro Hwy, North Campground at 2501. --Claude
